utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at 1D1101, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report from the National Security Service of Republika Srpska from Ilidza informing you, informing their minister and others that the Green Berets are located in the elementary school Petar Dokic in Cengic Vila where the headquarters of this formation is located as well. Do you remember that there was a correspondence between you and the MUP of Republika Srpska and the State Security Service and that they informed you about the information that was available to them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Before you answer the question, General. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Before the General answers, this date's from 25 May 1992, when the General was not in Sarajevo, and he said that repeatedly in his testimony. He's talked about his tour of duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And in addition to that query, on what basis do you say this was sent to the General while I don't see any such notation from the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that it was personally addressed to the General, Your Excellency, but certainly it was addressed to his security service because such a correspondence was obligatory.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may supplement that. If you remember, Mr. President, I said that I had some information about the existence of a command post. I was not aware of this document, to be honest, but somehow I remember that some sort of command post was there and this document confirms that. Just an observation on my part, nothing else. In Cengic Vila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you repeat your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, you arrived when, two months after this?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know, did your service receive or exchange information with the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did exchange information and informed me about what was important. But what is at stake here is that how this is phrased here and how the disposition of the forces is formulated, they're not changed on a daily basis. They remain for longer periods in specific locations, and I did have some information. I have no idea, but I told you earlier, a few days ago, in my testimony, that I had this piece of information that there was some sort of command post there. I did not remember any specific report but this is just a confirmation of what I said then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3513, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D7388, can we look at that one now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, we can zoom in onto the Serbian version alone. This is an order from the commander of the 3rd Motorised Brigade of the 1st Corps --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We don't have a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The translation of the English is incomplete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will represent -- I will present the document and the witness can control me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Motorised Brigade orders on the 13th of March 1993 replacement of hand defence grenades, and it says to collect all bombs without safety levers and send them to the logistical battalion Valter Peric, location Stup-Azici, and the depot in the kindergarten at Cengic Vila which has been converted into a depot of the MES, which means mines and explosives. That's right. This kindergarten, does it then become a legitimate military target, General?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, during the direct examination we discussed about what I told UNPROFOR to warn the 1st Corps of the BH Army, namely, not to use schools, kindergartens and similar facilities. The previous example and this one as well indicates that they did use kindergartens and schools to store mines and explosives there, just like the depot there in Dobrinja. And then, in such circumstances, it would become a military target, without any doubt. If there are children inside, then it should be avoided but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be MFI'd, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI'd D3514, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It was suggested to you that at Ciglane were a civilian settlement and you said that in Ciglane there were also some tanks which were stationed there and also other pieces of equipment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D193 is a document that I would like us to look at. D193. So it's a Defence document, 193.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, in paragraph 2 we see that in the tunnel in Velesici a tank was stationed, and in front of the building of the so-called TO BiH in Ciglane, a tank and an APC were stationed. Was that also at the time when you took over the corps command?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will again refer to the examination-in-chief when I discussed Ciglane and the surrounding area and when I mentioned the armoured battalion which was deployed in the area, and that a manoeuvre was conducted there. Whether they were going up towards Zuc, when there was a mechanised brigade -- the 1st Mechanised Brigade which was deployed somewhere, and whether this battalion was part of its composition, but in any case they were moving along this area in my time too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 2 briefly. Gornji Velesici are mentioned here on page 1. If we can please look at page 2 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, artillery weapons located on Hum below the relay and also at the firing range in Velesici. Did you know that there was a firing range there and that they were firing from there?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. President, I -- excuse me, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, what did you want to say, Mr. Galic?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wanted to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect, this is now redirect and I think Dr. Karadzic is really leading with the document. The untranslated document was an exception because Dr. Karadzic was putting that on the record for all of us, but he's really leading with the document and that should be discouraged, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you follow, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I can ask General whether he knows what was located in Hum below the relay and whether he is aware that there was a firing range in Velesici and whether there were any military targets there.

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day, when I stated the disposition of the forces and so on, I said that the artillery of the BH Army 1st Corps was located at the foot of Hum. It can be checked but it's certainly true. As for Velesici, I did not mention the information then, whether that was any presence any or not, I don't remember that was very important, but I know that there was some sort of firing range in that area. What else was located there? Well, it's listed here. I cannot interpret it because I was not so well informed about this disposition, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you know about the use of private houses as military facilities by the 1st Corps of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, both sides, not just the BH Army. We all used, mainly in Sarajevo, privately owned houses, buildings, residential buildings, and all the other infrastructure that had been built. There was no time to make special military facilities except along confrontation lines. Some field facilities were built there such as roads, bunkers, communicating trenches, and so on. So in other words, such facilities were used, private homes and houses, certainly. Even when the residents were still there. In particular in the Muslim-populated area in the zone of the BH Army's 1st Corps. If the Serbs had lived in those houses, they were kicked out and the army would then move in and use such facilities. We remember that there were some attempts on our side in Grbavica, when Budo Obradovic, the president of the Executive Council, perished because he did not allocate a Muslim house to a soldier. So there were such attempts on our side as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last line of the first paragraph says that in Muslim houses around the airport, members of the BH Army are located, and then in the atomic shelter in Dobrinja 3 and also in the Sipad furniture store. You told us about houses. How about the furniture store and atomic shelter in Dobrinja? How does that fit in your experience and what you knew about the militarisation in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobrinja, as we have seen here, through the indictment and through my evidence and through Madam Prosecutor's questions, was very important during the war, during my case, and during your case. It has always been the focus of attention. I did mention the atomic shelter and I said it was used not for the accommodation of civilians but for billeting soldiers and accommodating cannons and other equipment. So this only confirms what I've already said. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my submission that's not only leading with the document further but it's a leading question suggesting Dobrinja was militarised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Militarisation or the nature of civilian settlement was raised during the cross, and after setting -- introducing some foundational question, putting some individual documents, the Chamber does not -- does not have any difficulty with it. So I will -- the Chamber will allow the Defence to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. And now I'd like to look at 65 ter 14731.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you were aware of a staff in the vicinity of Cengic Vila. We saw a document to that effect. And now can we look at the document that I've just called up? I'm interested in page 3. Can we first look at page 1 to see who drafted the document. This is English. However, in Serbian it says Major Per Brennskag, military observer, on the 16th of March, 1995. Who --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't think it's English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't think the document we see is in English. It's in a Scandinavian language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be an English version somewhere, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3, please. Page 18 in the document. Page 3 in what I have. Page 18 in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the beginning where it says that there's the 111th Brigade and 112th Brigade, and then line 2, paragraph 2, where it says the King Tvrtko Brigade with its staff in the vicinity of Cengic Vila. Did you know of the King Tvrtko Brigade? Whose unit was that?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be zoomed in? I can't see very well. Maybe it is not even important because I can answer your question anyway. Mr. President, what date is this? I apologise it's very important for me to know the date. I can't see it in the document. Do you have it? Can you be of assistance?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date is 16th March 1995. However, he gives an overview of the information that he has.

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is excellent. This is excellent. I needed the date to be able to provide you with a complete answer. I spoke about the brigade Kralj Tvrtko, or King Tvrtko, which is an HVO brigade. Before 1993 when it was disbanded, it was deployed around Stupsko Brdo, Stupsko Petlja and thereabouts, and when once it was disbanded -- I don't know whether it kept the name or not, I believe that they even changed the name. We can see that it was deployed in the vicinity of Cengic Vila, which is in the area that we already discussed. I don't know whether it has anything to do with the information that I shared with you earlier, however, this is a confirmation that the were indeed troops there. The Kralj Tvrtko Brigade, or the King Tvrtko Brigade, is an HVO brigade. They were mixed the Croats and Muslims at the time, the command staff was changed, and so on and so forth. It's really not important so I don't want to go into more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the 1st Glorious Olovo Brigade? Where is its staff? Where is Buca Potok? We will show you a map later on.

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are two Potoks or two brooks, but in any case this in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: But the General said he didn't even need to see the document to answer Dr. Karadzic's question, so I don't think he's actually said anything about the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that he's indicated that this confirms information that he has. I think that pages 16 and 17 of the English should be admitted. It's not necessary to admit the whole document. I note that it pertains to the summer of 1995, so you can consider that, but nevertheless, I think the witness indicated that it was consistent or confirmed information that he believed during his tour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. If the document -- if Your Honours are inclined to admit the document, then I would simply ask that the whole thing come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit those two pages shown to the witness. We do not see the need to admit it in its entirety. Shall we give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3515, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does Mr. Piletta-Zanin have to change his flight, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, he has to. There were a lot of ambiguous questions which have created an impression that has to be elaborated and light shed on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, it was suggested to you that you were quick to refute protests and objections by UNPROFOR with regard to some incidents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at D2586?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If an incident happened and if there were casualties, did you need deny that without checking or did you perhaps check first? Before you read the document could you please answer. Is it correct that you were quick to refute things without checking first as the Prosecutor alleged?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided an answer. I can repeat the same answer again without referring to the document, Mr. President. Whenever there was an objection or a protest, I would check first with my subordinated units. Under the circumstances that prevailed at -- that allowed me to check as much as I could, and I also took measures which were contingent on the conditions. That was my answer then and I'm repeating it now. I agree that that was an assertion by the Prosecutor. However, I had something to say with this regard and my opinion has been known from the beginning of my evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document. Do you remember that the command of the Ilidza Brigade was ordered to set up a commission? How does that tally with what you said? Was that an exception or what? How did that tally with your general position?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're asking me whether I remember this particular document, this particular order, I don't. However, now that I read it, I can say that this was drafted by Milosevic because this is his signature. I believe he was my deputy, of course, and there's no dilemma here whatsoever. This is exactly how things transpired. Milosevic would not let things go lightly. None of my chiefs did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to call up D3390. D3390. Defence 3390.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is your answer to Colonel Daveau [phoen]. We'll go to the next page to see that this was indeed your telegram. You answer that you did not have any troops at Colina Kapa. As for Borije and Hadzic Ravne, we have our own troops so it would not be logical for us to open fire on them. Under 5 it says that you have strict adhere to the order of the commander of the Main Staff. And under 6 you say when it comes to the fire that was opened on Hrid and Logavina Street, we did not establish responsibility because of the absence of the soldiers who were in charge of the combat assets in question. Why did you not refute the allegations lightly? As you see in bullet point 6, does it mean that you checked everything else?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This speaks about my character and the character of all my troops. We checked what we did, and if we didn't, we said why we didn't, and that we were not in a position to provide an appropriate answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we go to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Bullet point 8, you say here that -- or you admit that, by mistake, a shell was fired -- there is no translation but I'm going to read. Lukavicka Street, Muhameda Dzudze Street and Djure Jaksica Street were not shelled. There was just one shell that fell on Lukavicka road when the mortar asset was being repaired without due caution.

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from bullet point 8 that we said that this was -- that this was our shell which was fired from my position by mistake because of careless handling of weapons. It is not a sin to admit a mistake. Not admitting a mistake creates other problems, but it is also not good if mistakes are repeated. That's why we opened up to that mistake because we also at the same time sought ways to avoid a repetition of that mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir. You also received various situations with regard to civilian settlements. I would like to look at a document. However, you responded that the Serbian civilian settlements were also shelled. D346 is the following document I would like to see, and let's see what you implied when you said that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is it. Can we zoom in for the benefit of the General. I hope that the other participants can see the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, this is a Muslim document sent by the 1st Corps on the 20th of March, 1993. In the first paragraph where it says information about the enemy, which is the Serbs obviously --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes we can't see the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly where is Rogoj with regard to the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rogoj is a pass leading towards Kalinovik and Foca and it is some 30 kilometres away from Sarajevo, or thereabouts. This is a pass from the Foca valley in Herzegovina towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can we scroll up to look at bullet point 2 where it says: Information about our own forces, i.e., the forces of the 1st Corps. It says that they opened fire from 130-millimetre cannons with two shells; a 105-millimetre howitzer, four shells; and a 152-millimetre howitzer top with 22 shells on the requested targets of the command of 1st Corps. Chetniks responded to -- on the sectors of our weapons by firing four projectiles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, bear it in mind when you don't show the English page on the monitor, the interpreters do not have access to the English, so please read slow, very slow. Yes, what is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, it says here that you responded by opening fire -- or, rather, launching four shells on their sector where their assets were deployed. Why did you do that? Why didn't you open fire on another sector?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we look at the Operative Group Igman we can see what assets that they had at their disposal. There is a 130-millimetre cannon, a 105-millimetre howitzer, and a howitzer cannon, 152-millimetres. They launched 25 shells and so on and so forth. Let me stop there. Those are heavy pieces. The heaviest that we had on our strength. They launched 25 shells, as they put it themselves, and later on they said they didn't have weapons, they didn't have assets, they didn't have anything to defend themselves, and they didn't have anything to respond to our fire. And when we responded we only launched four projectiles. I don't know whether they were shells or what. I don't know what we responded with. Those targets were mostly in that area of the Igman Operative Group, from Igman towards Rogoj. I suppose we didn't have more projectiles, but we were in a situation when we didn't have enough of that type of ammunition. I've already told you that from the very beginning we didn't have enough ammunition. That's why I would like to go back to Madam Prosecutor's allegations that we had the VBRs, yes, we did, but we didn't have any ammunition. We could not launch a single projectile when I arrived because we didn't have any reserves. We did not have any supplies. While I was there, the VBR or multi-rocket launcher, we did not use it once. We did have them but we didn't have ammunition. I also said that we did not have any ammunition for the 72-millimetre recoilless cannons. We didn't have a single shell. And we can see here and as I already told you, the armed forces of the BiH Army had shells and assets. That would be my answer to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the 82-millimetres recoilless gun, I want to correct that, and please look at these two lines where it says that they fired five shells against Vojkovici village and the forestry school. Was the Vojkovici village a civilian settlement?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojkovici village, we said where it was before. It's on the slopes of Igman. To the right of it is Hrasnica. So it was a civilian settlement. There were no military facilities in the village itself that could be targeted. And the forestry school was in the area of Ilidza, as far as I remember, Mr. President. That was next to Stojcevac, up towards Stojcevac, that's the area where the forestry school was and it was there on its own.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I see what the time is and I think that you announced that you would need some minutes, so perhaps if it's the time to stop, I could stop now and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I said that I would need some minutes. I don't think I said that, but I remember General said that he was tired. It's time to adjourn for today. We'll continue tomorrow. But before that, yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Since we still have a few minutes and in order to facilitate everybody's work including the Registry, would it be possible to have some forecast for tomorrow's hearing so that I can plan my flight back? And I would also like to have more information about whether the General would have to return by plane or by car. You had some reservations about that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will come -- I will ask Mr. Karadzic how much he would need tomorrow, but as to the way in which the General is to be escorted back to the third country, it goes beyond the purview of the Tribunal as a whole, so I don't think we have a say with respect to that, but once it was raised, I think -- I hope it would be solved in a way that all the parties are happy with. That's all I can say at the moment. But, Mr. Karadzic, how long would you need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I will finish certainly before the end of first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: But if not now, I may ask you tomorrow, too, that I be allowed to see witnesses that accomplish their own testimony and that are in the Detention Unit with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I followed. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think that Dr. Karadzic is ask that you modify your order concerning the separation of General Galic from him at the Detention Unit so that the Detention Unit is authorised to allow them to meet after his testimony is concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we have -- we had similar experience with the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It was mentioned, but it was too late. By the time we had contact with the Detention Unit, the witness had already been gone, but they seem to indicate that they believe that unless your order is modified, since it does, you know, create a separation regime, that they would be unable to accommodate any visits between Dr. Karadzic and the detainee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the issue. Before we adjourn, Mr. Tieger, in relation to the Prosecution motion to exclude certain parts of Mr. Trivic's statement, the Defence responded that it had no objection to the deletion of pages 12 to 20, but -- although it stated that it would add some parts later on. In light of the response, are you ready to withdraw your motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We may be dealing with the subject further, but you're quite right in respect of events thus far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.52 p.m.,
